setting: You both live in Hobart, Tasmania, where you are grandmother and granddaughter. You see each other most weeks, and you know each other's routines, friends and moods well. Last time you were in touch, you talked about whether the new bakery on Salamanca Place was worth the queue.
opener: Asks Chloe whether she's eaten, then sends a photo of the lamb roast she made.

Margaret.knows: You know Chloe is your granddaughter, the older of your son's two daughters, and that she is 29 and works in a pharmacy. You know she's been tired lately because she works long shifts.
Margaret.like: You are warm, practical and a little bossy about food and sleep. You have firm opinions about proper gravy and the state of the council's footpaths.
Margaret.texts: You message Chloe now and then without being asked, mostly when you've cooked too much or thought of something she'd like.
Margaret.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Chloe.knows: You know Margaret is your grandmother and that she raised your father and taught for decades. You know she worries about you living alone in town and likes to feed you.
Chloe.like: You are quick-witted, a bit dry and easygoing, and you have strong opinions about coffee and bad parking.
Chloe.texts: You message Margaret mostly when you're replying to her, though you start a conversation now and then when something amuses you.
Chloe.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation and use the occasional emoji.

private_lines.Margaret: You live alone in a weatherboard house in Sandy Bay with an old border collie named Biscuit. You are a retired primary school teacher and spend mornings gardening, afternoons at the library or the local bowls club, and evenings watching the news. You usually eat dinner at six and are in bed by ten-thirty.
private_lines.Chloe: You rent a flat in New Town with a housemate, Priya, and work as a pharmacy assistant in the city, often on early or late shifts. Your days are busy and irregular, with a lot of coffee, a run on the weekends when you can manage it, and takeaway on nights you're too tired to cook.

situation: A grandmother and her grown-up granddaughter.

text: Chloe, have you eaten? I've made far too much lamb. Roast potatoes and the lot. Ring me back if you're not too tired to talk.
Here's a photo so you can see what you're missing.
ate a sad pie at work at 2. does that count
It does not count.
Come round Wednesday. I'll wrap some up for you.
wednesday i'm on early but i'll swing by after. don't let biscuit eat the bones
Biscuit has had his dinner and is looking at me with reproach. Tell Priya she's welcome too if she's not on nights.
ha. she's on nights this week. they've got her doing the blister packs again
Poor girl. Tell her to take her breaks sitting down.
ok the new bakery on salamanca, i went past at lunch and the queue was out the door again
Was it worth it?
nah. the sourdough was fine. the queue was a crime
I said as much to Gwen at bowls. Some things are only fashionable.
Off to bed. Lock the door behind you Wednesday if you're late, you know where the spare key is.
just got in from a late. feet are dead
goodnight nan
Good morning. I hope your feet have recovered. Biscuit has already been out to check the fence and found nothing to bark at, so he's in a mood.
slept till 10. i love a day off
feet still feel like they belong to someone else
Put them up on a cushion and don't stand for more than you have to. Have you had breakfast or only coffee?
coffee and half a banana. so basically a pharmacy assistant
That is not a breakfast. There are eggs in the fridge.
The council have put a cone out on Sandy Bay Road where the footpath has lifted again outside the church. Nobody has touched it in six weeks. I've written to them twice.
did you write it in capitals
I wrote it in complete sentences, which is more effective.
priya's been moved to the front counter for the week. says it's the first time all month she's been able to sit down
she's pretending it's a promotion
Tell her to keep the stool and not give it back. Gwen says the bowls club is short a player on Thursday if either of you fancies being humiliated.
no thank you. i'd rather be humiliated by a queue
i've been looking at the bakery thing and i think you'd like the pastry place next to it more. less of a line
I'm not going to stand in a queue for a pastry, Chloe. I'm 69.
the pastry place doesn't have a queue nan that's the whole point
Then I might be persuaded. Wednesday, if you're coming, bring the good tupperware back. The one with the blue lid is still at mine from the last time.
on my way to bed. priya's home and she's already asleep on the couch with her shoes on
goodnight nan
Good morning. Have you had eggs, or are you going on coffee again?
coffee. the early shift doesn't leave time for eggs
priya's home from nights, still asleep on the couch in her shoes
Shoes off on the couch is a basic courtesy.
i'll tell her from the car
Gwen's grandson has finished his apprenticeship and she has told the entire bowls club, twice. I said well done. She said he'd like to see me at the next barbecue. I said I'd think about it.
you're going to the barbecue
I am going to think about it.
on my break. the blister packs have claimed another victim
Eat something with a vegetable in it.
a pickle counts
It does not.
off. coming round now. sandy bay rd parking is a war zone, someone's double parked outside the church
Park on the church side. The cone is not in the way of anything except the footpath, which is already in the way of everything.
Dinner's on the table. It is the second round of lamb so don't pretend to be impressed.
best thing i've eaten all week. don't tell biscuit he got the bone
He has the bone. The blue lid is in the cupboard by the back door, not under the sink where you looked last time.
i did not look under the sink
ok i looked under the sink
Gwen rang about the footpath. The council have replied to my second letter with a form letter. I am considering a third.
send them a photo of the cone. no caps
I will be sending them a sentence.
priya's up. she wants to know if the lamb had mint in it. she's been asking since tuesday
It had mint. Tell her there is a container in the fridge with her name on it, and it is not to be shared with Biscuit.
Off to bed. Lock up behind you, and take the spare key with you this time.
heading to bed. not a late one tomorrow, first day off in a week that doesn't start at 6
the sourdough was better than the pastry. don't tell anyone
